title: Crypto
subtitle: Digests, message authentication & random bytes.
intro: Compute cryptographic digests and HMACs directly from SQL values. Use secure random bytes for tokens and salts, or aggregate values in a specified order for reproducible checksums.

reference.name: crypto_hash(algorithm, value)
reference.description: Return a digest as BLOB; algorithm is a string.

reference.name: crypto_hmac(algorithm, key, message)
reference.description: Authenticate a message with a secret key; returns BLOB.

reference.name: crypto_random_bytes(length)
reference.description: Generate the requested number of cryptographically secure random bytes.

reference.name: crypto_hash_agg(algorithm, value ORDER BY ...)
reference.description: Aggregate values into a digest with explicit input order.

reference.name: to_hex(blob) / lower(text)
reference.description: Format binary digests as printable lowercase hexadecimal.

notes.title: Choose the algorithm explicitly
notes.body: Common names include blake3, blake2b-512, sha2-256, sha2-512 and sha3-256. MD5 and SHA-1 are legacy choices, unsuitable for collision-resistant security.

notes.title: A checksum needs a data contract
notes.body: Specify row order, input types and serialization. A digest of one field is not automatically an unambiguous digest of a whole row. Fast hashes are a separate hashfuncs extension.

examples.title: Bytes & ordered aggregates
examples.caption: ORDER BY belongs inside the aggregate call for reproducible ordering.

assertions: SELECT CASE WHEN lower(to_hex(crypto_hash('sha2-256','hello')))='2cf24dba5fb0a30e26e83b2ac5b9e29e1b161e5c1fa7425e73043362938b9824' AND octet_length(crypto_random_bytes(32))=32 AND lower(to_hex(crypto_hmac('sha2-256','example-key','message')))='1f2911120d44895ac2ef32a5546d4591bca63c8874b25bb2d3085b62f6c084b8' THEN true ELSE error('crypto outputs') END;
